description: The Department of the Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center Carderock Division (NSWCCD), announces Solicitation No. N0016727R0005 (previously N0016726R1009) for the Environmental and Ship Motion Forecasting Follow-On (ESMF FO) program. This requirement is being solicited as a full and open competition. The Government intends to award one single-award, Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year ordering period. To access the solicitation and available attachments, prospective offerors shall refer to the attachments and links associated with this notice. * Attachments 01 through 06 are subject to Distribution Statement D and are authorized for distribution only to the Department of Defense and U.S. DoD contractors. To request and receive these attachments, prospective offerors must possess an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) and a verified, active Joint Certification Program (JCP) certification supported by an approved DD Form 2345. JCP information is available at https://www.public.dacs.dla.mil/jcp/ext/#. * Prospective offerors requesting Attachments 01 through 06 shall submit their request to Joseph Estrella at Joseph.l.estrella.civ@us.navy.mil, with copies to Michael L. Jones at michael.l.jones5.civ@us.navy.mil and William Finke at william.g.finke.civ@us.navy.mil. The request email shall include the companys CAGE Code and use the following subject line: N0016726R1009. [Insert Company Name]. title: Container-Based Fire Training Facility
description:
The Cantonal Fire Police Authority of Schaffhausen intends to construct a new firefighter training facility in CH-8222 Beringen (Canton of Schaffhausen, Switzerland).

The facility will be constructed largely using shipping containers. To ensure the full functionality of the training facility, the shipping containers must be modified accordingly.

This contract covers the supply of the shipping containers, including the necessary modifications to each individual container.

Depending on the specific requirements, these modifications may include the installation of doors, windows with shutters, the alteration or installation of partition walls, and the creation of openings in the side walls.

description: Les principales prestations de l'accord-cadre à bons de commande sont décrites ci-après : Pour des projets de construction d’installations nucléaires ou de travaux de modifications d’installations individuelles et d’ICPE (Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement) en exploitation ou en démantèlement : • réalisation d’études, d’analyses, de bilans, de documents de synthèse et de dossiers réglementaires de sûreté nucléaires, et contribution à leur instruction par les autorités concernées ; • définition et gestion de la remontée de conformité au travers des exigences de sûreté ; • gestion de la configuration sûreté des installations en lien avec l’ingénierie système (outils/processus spécifiques, gestion du référentiel et des outils de gestion d’événements) ; • élaboration et mise en œuvre d’outils et de processus d’ingénierie de sûreté transverses ; • management et animation des équipes. L’exécution des prestations pourra se faire sur les différents sites de la DAM ainsi que sur la base navale de Toulon. Le marché comporte : • une phase de réversibilité entrante de 6 mois (optionnelle) ; • une phase de « production » composée de 36 mois fermes et 36 mois optionnels ; • une phase de réversibilité sortante concomitante sur les 6 derniers mois de la phase « production » en cours (optionnelle).

title: Protected Anti-Jam Tactical SATCOM (PATS) Operations Center (PATSOC) Mission Operations Services Request for Information (RFI)
description: Section I: PTES Description & Background Protected Anti-Jam Tactical SATCOM (PATS) provides worldwide, beyond line of sight (BLOS), Anti-Jam, Low Probability of Intercept (LPI) communications to tactical warfighters in both benign and contested environments. PATS uses the Protected Tactical Waveform (PTW) to enable forward-deployed users and coalition/international partners to fill capability gaps for protected communications. PATS employs a military web-based planning and operations architecture and communications hubs to enable existing or new terminals with a PTW-capable modem. The PTW can be used on any PTW processed or non-processed wideband satellite communications platform, providing mission critical communications with varying levels of protection depending on the SATCOM environment, satellite system, and available resources. PTW supports high throughput in benign conditions and adapts automatically to reduced capacity in favor of increased robustness for contested environments such as jamming, terminal movement, and weather degradation. PTW also provides logical and cryptographic separation of user groups to maintain operational security. PATS will be implemented in phases aligned with Protected Tactical Enterprise Service (PTES) ground capabilities. PTES is the enabling ground component of PATS, providing operational planning, mission and network management, and hubs for PTW networks using Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS) and commercial transponded SATCOM systems. WGS PATS Phase capability provides PTW over WGS, and Commercial Satellite Communications (COMSATCOM) Phase increases flexibility and resiliency by supporting PTW over COMSATCOM. Protected Tactical Satellite (PTS) Phase adds PTW over PTS satellites for near-peer jamming protection. Section II: RFI Objective The purpose of this RFI is to understand industry capabilities, risks, staffing approaches, recommended contract structure, transition considerations, and relevant experience associated with delivering mission planning and mission operations described in this request. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued to identify and gather information from sources capable of providing full-spectrum staffing for the Protected Anti-Jam Tactical SATCOM (PATS) Operations Center (PATSOC). The Government seeks information regarding industry capability to establish, staff, train, manage, and sustain a cleared operational workforce supporting planning, provisioning, monitoring, management, cybersecurity coordination, operational reporting, and execution of PTW networks. Government anticipates utilizing contractor personnel to fulfill designated onsite operator positions for each phase of performance, as discussed in Section III, Table 1, below. The anticipated NAICS for this acquisition is 517810 and the size standard is $40,000,000.00. Small businesses and Government entities with existing contract vehicles are encouraged to respond to this request. Section III: RFI Scope The contractor shall be responsible for management oversight and for providing qualified and cleared personnel. The contractor shall conduct proficiency and recurring training, maintaining situational awareness of COI processes and procedures regarding mission planning and mission operations, updating training, technical manuals, TTPs, continuity planning, and any relevant material required to perform mission planning and mission operations accordingly. The contractor shall staff the PATSOC and conduct mission planning and mission operations using Government-provided MMS, NMS, KMS, PATS PVT, and associated applications, while interfacing with additional tools required to perform and support mission planning and mission operations. PATSOC personnel are expected to manage account administration, registrar functions, role-based access control enabling mission planning and mission operations. These functions will extend to the COI enabling the concept of operations. The contractor may support phases of the operational lifecycle, including pre-operational test preparation, IT&E/MOT&E support, discrepancy report and problem report resolution, regression testing, transition to CFC Trial Period operations, sustained operational execution, situational awareness reporting, Continuity of Operations preparation and execution, and transition to a future operations and maintenance construct. The Government anticipates that the phases of support described herein may be revised, restructured, or further subdivided based on industry responses to this RFI. Pre-Mission Operations shall prepare for mission objectives defined in the PATS Concept of Operations (CONOPS), and the PTES Capability Development Document (CDD). The following summary is provided to clarify the focus of the anticipated Pre-Operations Mission Support phase. Beginning after PATSOC Site Acceptance and approximately 90 days prior to the IT&E dry-run event and continuing until the start of the CFC Trial Period. Develop and submit a PATSOC Staffing Plan identifying proposed roles, responsibilities, and staffing quantities for the Pre-Operations Mission Support period. Operate, evaluate, and use the Mission Management System (MMS), PATS Planning Verification Tool (PVT), Network Management System (NMS), Key Management System (KMS) and associated applications for network/mission planning, product generation, monitoring, management, trouble ticket response, network management, account management, registrar functions, and COI situational awareness. title: France – Construction work for bridges and tunnels, shafts and subways – LOT 1 Travaux de terrassement, de fabrication et pose d’éléments de 3 lignes de galeries secondaires du RSGE
description: Avant de réaliser les travaux de construction des ouvrages de stockage de déchets radioactifs sur le Centre de stockage de l’Aube (CSA), il convient de procéder à la mise en place des galeries sous ouvrages. Ces galeries souterraines (éléments préfabriqués) ont notamment pour fonction principale de permettre l’accès sous les ouvrages pendant les phases d’exploitation et de surveillance du site (d’une durée minimale de 300 ans) afin de faire des contrôles des éventuels écoulements issus des ouvrages de stockage qui sont récupérés dans un réseau spécifique appelé « Réseau Séparatif Gravitaire Enterré » (RSGE) implanté dans ces galeries. Ces galeries sont réalisées sous les interlignes des lignes d’ouvrages, une galerie desservant 2 lignes d’ouvrages contigus. Les travaux objet du présent avis de marché comprennent principalement : • Les travaux de terrassement de grande masse pour un volume estimatif de 20000m3, • Les travaux de terrassement pour un volume estimatif de 75000m3 de sable notamment pour la mise en place des 3 galeries enterrées, • La démolition de longrines dans l’emprise de la zone de creusement, • La fourniture et la pose de 3 lignes de galeries préfabriquées sur approximativement 265ml et des canalisations intérieures. La dimension intérieure de chaque élément de galerie est d’environ 2m50 en hauteur et 1m30 en largeur. • La reconstruction des tronçons de jonction avec la galerie principale, • La fourniture des longueurs droites des canalisations du RSGE et des piézomètres, • Le rabattement de la nappe pendant les travaux, • La substitution des sols en place par un remblai en sable avec les matériaux du site • Le remblaiement des excavations exécutées pour la pose des galeries jusqu’aux cotes prescrites sur les plans guides de remblai, • La fourniture et la mise en œuvre d’un béton de rattrapage sur le toit des galeries pour établir le plan horizontal de fondation des longrines inter-ouvrages, • La note de calculs d’exécution des éléments de galerie principale (coulés en place, ou préfabriqués partiellement), • La note de calculs d’exécution des différents éléments et clavages de galerie inter-ouvrages, • La note de calcul du dispositif de rabattement de nappe, montrant en particulier la conformité avec les exigences liées au bac de décantation, • Les plans d’exécutions des terrassements et des remblaiements, figurant notamment les réseaux permettant la maîtrise des eaux pluviales après le chantier, • Les plans de coffrage et de ferraillage des éléments de galerie inter-ouvrages, • Les plans de coffrage et de ferraillage des tronçons de galerie principale à reconstituer, • Les plans de coffrage et de ferraillage des clavages, • Les plans d’implantation des pointes filtrantes, • Les plans d’exécutions des ouvrages de serrurerie : trappe de fermeture, échelle de sortie en extrémité des galeries inter-ouvrages et marche pour accès dans la galerie principale. L’Andra étant certifiée ISO 9001, ISO 14001 et ISO 45001, le titulaire mettra en place, pour l’exécution de ses missions, une organisation de modèle « ISO 9001, version 2015, notamment en matière : - De gestion des compétences, - De gestion de la documentation, - De traitement des non-conformités. Au titre des dispositions prises pour le contrôle de ses travaux, le titulaire est tenu de : - De formaliser et programmer les actions de contrôle appropriées, - De faire effectuer ces contrôles par du personnel qualifié, - De prouver que les contrôles sont effectués, - De démontrer que les prestations sont conformes aux spécifications. Pour les prestations réalisées sur le CSA, le titulaire prend en compte les exigences de l’arrêté du 7 février 2012. Cet arrêté fixe les règles générales relatives aux installations nucléaires de base. Le titulaire devra la totalité des procédures d’exécution et de contrôle du Plan Qualité nécessaires à l’exécution des travaux. Les procédures à établir sont au minimum : - Procédure d’entreposage et de gestion des produits dangereux et inflammables, - Procédure d’élimination des déchets produits sur le chantier avec les dispositions préparatoires suivantes : - La liste des centres de stockage et de regroupement ou des unités de recyclage ou des lieux de réutilisation où seront acheminés les différents déchets à évacuer, - Les méthodes qui seront employées pour ne pas mélanger les différents déchets, - Procédures en usine comprenant : - Procédure de mise en place des éléments de galerie sur parc de stockage en usine et/ou sur chantier, - Procédure de finitions et réparations en cas de petits défauts en usine et sur site, - Procédure de démolitions, d’excavations et remblaiement : - Procédure d’exécution des rabattements de nappe comprenant le suivi des débits et la mesure des quantités de sable décanté, - Procédure d’exécutions des excavations, - Procédure de démolition des longrines et amorces de longrines et des regards en tête de ligne, - Procédure d’exécution des dépôts de matériaux sur le Centre de l’Aube, - Procédure d’exécution du remblaiement des fouilles, - Procédure de réalisation des enrobés, - Procédure de réalisation des galeries : - Procédure d’exécution des galeries coulées en place ou partiellement préfabriquées, - Procédure d’exécution des clavages de galerie principale, - Procédure de pose de galerie inter-ouvrages, - Procédure de réparation en cas de défaut d’étanchéité, - Procédure de réalisation du béton de rattrapage sur les galeries, - Procédure de pose du complexe d’argile gonflante (orégonite) au droit des joints. - Procédure des contrôles à réaliser sur les éléments de galeries (en usine, à réception sur chantier, durant la phase de mise en œuvre et à la reconstitution des sols pour les opérations de terrassement, - Procédure de stockage des éprouvettes destinées aux essais du béton de rattrapage, - … Les étapes de la procédure et les modalités de sélection des candidats sont décrites au chapitre 2 du Règlement de consultation de procédure avec negociation.

description: 693JJ327BAA0002 FORMERLY 693JJ326BAA0006 This BAA is an expression of interest only and does not commit the Government to pay any proposal preparation costs. The Government reserves the right to award or to not award contracts or other instruments determined to be of benefit to the Government in achieving the goals of this program. The EAR Program addresses the need to conduct research on longer term and higher risk breakthrough topics with the potential for transformational improvements to plan, build, renew, and operate safe, congestion free, and environmentally sound transportation systems. Your response must address capabilities specific to the services required in the attached PWS and must include the following: Interested Vendors shall at a minimum, provide the following information in the initial paragraph of the submission: Name of Company Address Point of Contact Phone Number Fax Number Email address Company Business Size and Status NAICS code(s) Socioeconomic data Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Number Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC) Provide a summary of your capability to meet the requirements contained within the draft PWS for the following areas: Can a single SaaS/COTS solution meet all PWS requirements across the five capabilities (Workflows, Document Review, Hearings, DCD, and BIR)? Would a single prime contract or modular acquisition yield better value and manageable integration risk? What are the key benefits, risks, and trade-offs of integrating multiple SaaS/COTS solutions versus developing a single custom application, considering user experience, integration complexity, auditability, release coordination, testing, support, total cost of ownership, and end-to-end contractor accountability, while maximizing SaaS/COTS capabilities, minimizing custom development, and ensuring seamless integration without manual hand-offs, duplicate data entry, or a fragmented user experience for Board personnel? (PWS: 3.2; 5) Can all five capabilities be delivered as vendor-hosted SaaS without VA-provided hardware, VAEC compute/storage, or middleware? For any VA-hosted elements, identify sizing, hosting boundary, connectivity, security authorization, support ownership, and estimated Government costs. (PWS: 3.2; 5.2.1.1; 5.2.1.7; 6.1) What are the capabilities of workflows, routing rules, fields, templates, and reports that VA business administrators can configure or modify without vendor development or intervention? Identify any limitations, risks, training, or dependencies associated with administrator-managed changes, including governance and approval requirements, testing and validation, rollback capabilities, release lead times, support implications, and licensing constraints. (PWS: 3.3; 5.2.2.6; 5.2.5.1) Can the Document Review/Reader (eDiscovery) capability be deployed before other capabilities and without integration with the existing Caseflow system? If so, describe the interim approach for user access, case association, document retrieval, permissions, annotations, search, and navigation. Identify the earliest feasible deployment timeframe, prerequisites, risks, limitations, and potential rework required for future integration. (PWS: 4.2; 5.2.3; 5.3; 5.4) Identify native capabilities and those requiring separate tools for OCR, handwriting recognition, duplicate detection, classification, annotation, relevance assessment, and summarization. Explain how existing OCR text and metadata can be ingested from third-party repositories to avoid unnecessary reprocessing. Address accuracy validation, source citations, human-in-the-loop controls, auditability, privacy protections, and per-page or per-transaction costs, distinguishing ingestion costs from new OCR processing costs. (PWS: 5.2.1.8; 5.2.3.5) What is a reasonable timeline to achieve full production deployment and migration of Caseflow and VACOLS? Is VA s target of within 12 months feasible? Assess the feasibility of an accelerated implementation, including integration, VA ATO, data migration, testing, training, and cutover. Provide a realistic timeline with key milestones, dependencies, risks, and opportunities to accelerate delivery. Identify the earliest achievable date for full operational capability and any factors that could delay implementation. If the 12-month target is not feasible, identify the limiting constraints and propose an alternative timeline, including key milestones and assumptions. (PWS: 4.1 4.2; 5.3 5.4) What milestone-based payment structure would you recommend? Discuss common commercial payment terms for implementation and deployment of an enterprise-wide solution of similar size and complexity for a federal agency. Describe the proposed milestone-based payment schedule for building and deploying this solution, identifying the measurable deliverables and VA acceptance criteria that would trigger payment at each stage, including development, integration, migration, testing, and production deployment. Recommend when SaaS licensing and operational charges should begin for phased releases to avoid production-level costs during development, minimize VA financial risk, and incentivize full deployment within 12 months or sooner. (PWS: 4.1 4.2) Describe your approach for migrating active and historical Caseflow/VACOLS data, including records, task and state transformations, identifiers, histories, roles, hearings, decisions, and annotations. Address the estimated duration, level of effort, constraints, common causes of delay, and key risks. Explain how you would execute cutover while maintaining service availability, minimizing parallel operation of legacy and new systems, and avoiding carryover of legacy system dependencies. (PWS: 5.4; Appendix A; Appendices C G) Describe the current security and authorization status of each proposed product, including compliance gaps, required remediation, and realistic timelines for VA ATO approval and network connectivity. Per VA guidance, proposed solutions are not required to be FedRAMP authorized but must meet applicable NIST and VA security requirements and obtain a VA Authority to Operate (ATO). List any current security frameworks that the products have (FedRAMP, StateRAMP, NIST, SOC-2, current governmental ATO s, etc) Identify any PWS security requirements that need clarification or unnecessarily restrict commercial solutions while maintaining mandatory federal and VA security controls. (PWS: 5.2.1.5; 5.8; 6.1 6.3) Identify up to five recommended PWS changes, expected effect on competition and cost, and additional information VA should provide to support a reliable proposal. For recommendations, cite the PWS section, provide specific replacement targets or wording, and explain cost, schedule, security, operational, and competition implications. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. title: Annual Bulk Petroleum Purchase for Atlantic, Europe, and Mediterranean Region
description: 11/23/2026 Update: The solicitation closing time listed in Sam.gov has been updated to 1PM EST. The closing date remains unchanged at December 21, 2027. The updated closing time and date now align with the offer due date time specified on the SF1449. This is the solicitation for the annual bulk fuel procurement for the Atlantic/Europe/Mediterranean (AEM) 2027 Purchase Program. See attachment/links section for full request for proposals and all attachments. The fuel procured from this buy will cover various locations in the AEM geographic region. The NAICS code for this procurement is 324110. The solicitation closing date and time is December 21, 2027, at 1PM EST. The Program's Ordering Period is date of award through June 30, 2028. The Delivery Period is July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2028, with a 30-day carryover period. Delivery modes will be by tanker and pipeline. FOB Destination tanker offers will not be accepted. The requirements may increase during the delivery period and be met by supplemental solicitations tied to this procurement. DLA Energy will be using the Bulk Offer Entry Tool (OET) for this Procurement. The usage of the Bulk OET is mandatory. The Bulk OET will allow Offerors to electronically submit and sign their offer (including the SF1449). If you have any questions, please email Paul Johnson at paul.johnson@dla.mil., Jamillah Kinard at Jamillah.Kinard@dla.mil, or Gerardo Gomez at Gerardo.Gomez@dla.mil.

title: U.S. Mission San Jose, Costa Rica Local Guard Services
description: QUESTIONS DUE: NOVEMBER 30, 2026 AT 1:00 PM EST PROPOSALS DUE: DECEMBER 21, 2026 AT 1:00 PM EST The U.S. Department of State (DOS) has a requirement for a qualified Contractor to provide Local Guard Services to support the U.S. Mission San Jose, Costa Rica. The Government requires a secure environment to conduct their mission. The Contractor shall provide the organizational structure, management, and qualified staff at levels adequate to meet or exceed the requirement contained in the Performance Work Statement. The Contractor shall be required to provide services in a manner that prevent loss or injury to U.S. personnel, dependents, property; destruction of assets; to prevent unauthorized access; and deter potential terrorist attacks. Anticipated period of performance is one base year and four one-year options (to be exercised at the sole discretion of the Government). See attached 19AQMM27R0032 for more details. For Restricted Access, please return a completed Restricted Access Form to the Contracting Officer, Sara M. Marron, at MarronSM2@state.gov and then request access in sam.gov. The Government will provide a PowerPoint as an attachment to this solicitation in lieu of a site visit. Vendors shall use the question format Excel document provided and follow the instructions as outlined in Section L. PHONE CALLS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED.

REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. AFMETCAL is seeking sources to procure and deliver Tire Inflator Calibrators. The Tire Inflator Calibrator (TIC) is a rugged diagnostic system used to test, verify, and calibrate the accuracy of hand-held pneumatic tire inflator kits. These inflator kits are critical for maintaining correct tire pressures across the aircraft fleet, and the calibrator ensures their built-in pressure gauges and relief valves read and perform correctly. The Air Force Metrology and Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) is seeking to procure up to 76 units of this system to support calibration operations. The system consists of two primary operational areas: a Supply Section and a Measurement Section. The Supply Section connects directly to a workshop air source and uses a pressure gauge, a safety relief valve, and a fine-tuning metering valve to deliver a precise, controlled stream of air into the tire inflator assembly being tested. The Measurement Section then receives the air released from the tire inflator assembly. It routes this air through an isolation valve into a specialized chamber (which acts as a mock "tire" to simulate realistic air expansion) and measures it using highly accurate digital pressure gauges. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity is 76 units over 6 years. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. title: Multi-Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities on DDG-51 Class Ships Homeported in Norfolk, VA
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N00024-26-R-4439 to procure a series of Multiple Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities (ISRAs) on DDG-51 Class ships homeported in Norfolk, VA. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Governments facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. title: Evaluations, Assessments, and Support Services (EASS)
description: You are invited to submit a proposal in response to the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Langley Research Center (LaRC) Evaluations, Assessments, and Support Services (EASS) solicitation. The principal purpose of this requirement is to acquire support services for the Science Office for Mission Assessments (SOMA), located at NASA Langley Research Center. SOMA is responsible for the management and oversight of evaluations, assessments, analyses, and other support services for the NASA Headquarters Science Mission Directorate (SMD). The scope includes proposal/Phase A reports; evaluations for SMD Announcements of Opportunity (AO) flight investigations; assessments for independent reviews of investigations and programs; analyses related to assessment and evaluations; and other contractor support services as specified in individual Task Orders (TOs). The EASS procurement is essential for the advancement of the NASA Science Plan, A Vision for Scientific Excellence. This contract directly supports SOMA and SMD. The contractor ensures that all work is objective and meets all requirements regarding organizational and personal conflicts of interest and limitations of future contracting as defined by this contract and as further defined in individual TOs where necessary. This contract supports NASA�s most urgent and important science needs, and without this contract, SMD would be unable to execute its extensive scientific commitments and achieve NASA�s science priorities. See attached Final RFP Cover Letter and Final RFP documents for full details.

title: Design/Build Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR), Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) 21, JBMDL, NJ
description: 10/08/2026: ***Anticipated Solicitation Date, Solicitation Number as well as building description have been updated*** 08/30/2026: ***Anticipated Solicitation Date as well as building description has been updated*** ***THE SOLICITATION NUMBER HAS BEEN UPDATED TO W912QR27RA004*** DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) W912QR27RA004 for the Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) 21 at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst (JBMDL) in Burlington, New Jersey. The project will repair failing facility components and extend the economic life of the facility by 25 years, providing a modern maintenance facility that enables readiness for the Army Reserve units located in the surrounding area. The project scope includes the repair of the failing HVAC and electrical systems, the removal of non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspaces as required, the repair/replacement/upgrade of light fixtures with code compliant units, the installation of a code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, and the repair of electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. The project also repairs the exterior structural elements, replaces the failing standing seam metal roof, and corrects all life safety deficiencies while maintaining the elements of the building's exterior. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. All hazardous materials (HAZMAT) removed as part of the demolition will be disposed of following all state and federal guidelines. The Contract Duration is one thousand ninety-five (1,095) calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed. TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition will be a 100%Total Small Business Set-Aside. SELECTION PROCESS: This will be a two-phase Design/Build procurement process. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best Value Tradeoff source selection process. Potential offerors are invited to submit their performance, technical, and capability information as will be described in section 00 22 16 of the Solicitation, for review and consideration by the Government. The selection process for Phase I will evaluate such factors (not necessarily in order): Past Performance and Technical Approach for Design/Build. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation Following completion of the evaluation of Phase I, a target of five (5) of the most highly qualified offerors will be invited to participate in Phase II. The selected offerors for Phase II will be invited to submit additional information as will be described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Management Plan, and Price. Standard Form (SF) 1442 will also be required. (NOTE: The evaluation factors for Phase II are subject to change with the Phase II amendment.) All evaluation factors, other than cost or price, are considered approximately equal to cost or price. DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussion should it be deemed in the Government's best interest. CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. ANTICIPATED SOLICITATION RELEASE DATE: The Government anticipates releasing the solicitation on or about 30 October 2026 and approximate closing date on or about 30 November 2026. Actual dates and times will be identified in the solicitation. Responses to this synopsis are not required. Additional details can be found in the solicitation when it is posted. This notice will be updated if the anticipated soliciation release date extends beyond 30 October 2026. SITE VISIT: A site visit will be held following the issuance of the Phase II solicitation to the Offerors selected to move forward. The exact location and time will be included in the solicitation. SOLICITATION WEBSITE: The official solicitation, when posted, will be available free of charge by electronic posting only and may be found at federal Contracting Opportunities website, https://sam.gov. Paper copies of the solicitation will not be issued. Telephone, email, and Fax requests for this solicitation will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the website for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the website periodically for any amendments to the solicitation. REGISTRATIONS: Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database: System to for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right award to the next prospective Offeror. POINT-OF-CONTACT: The point-of-contact for this procurement is Contract Specialist, Mr. Seth Dukes at seth.j.dukes@usace.army.mil.

title: Multi-Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities on DDG-51 Class Ships Homeported in Norfolk, VA
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N00024-26-R-4439 to procure a series of Multiple Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities (ISRAs) on DDG-51 Class ships homeported in Norfolk, VA. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Governments facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. This solicitation is issued electronically via PIEE and interested offerors should monitor PIEE and SAM.gov for any applicable solicitation amendments, thereafter. This posting does not include all relevant attachments. Potential offerors will need to request access to the attachments by providing a written request to the Contract Specialist, Alicia Vesey, at alicia.m.vesey.civ@us.navy.mil and the Contracting Officer, Paul Kang, at paul.k.kang.civ@us.navy.mil. Include your company SAM UEI number with the request so contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management. These attachments will be transmitted via DoD SAFE. To receive access to Attachment J-2 (Work Item Plans, Drawings and Other References}, including references that contain limiting distribution statements, provide a written request to the Mid-Atlantic Regional Maintenance Center (MARMC) Technical Librarian, Timothy Russell at timothy.russell1.civ@us.navy.mil with a copy to the Contract Specialist and the Contracting Officer listed above. Include your company SAM UEI number with the request so that contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management. AMENDMENT 0001: The purpose of this amendment is to make the following changes: 1) Make updates to Section B (Notes B.1, G.5d-f, and J.2); 2) Make updates to Section C (Paragraphs 1.4 and 1.12); 3) Add clause 52.217-9 to Section I; 4) Provide responses to Gate 1 Bidders Questions submitted via Attachment J-3; 5) Extend the Due Date for Bidders Questions Set 3 to 09 November 2026 (Section L.I.C); 6) Extend the Proposal Due Date to 21 December 2026 (Section L.II.A); 7) Add clauses L-204-H003, L-209-H009, L-211-H001, L-215-H004, and L-219-H001 to Section L; 8) Add clause M-247-H001 to Section M. Reference discs (Attachment J-2) are still under development. Offerors will be notified via an amendment as to when Attachment J-2 can be requested from the Technical Librarian.

title: J041--FY27 NRM | 460-26-011 - CON Replace West Entrance Return Air Gan | NCO 4 Construction East (VA-26-00069614)
description: VA Medical Center Wilmington intends to issue a construction contract. The project consists of: The Contractor shall provide all labor, transportation, materials, equipment, and supervision required for Replace West Entrance Return Air Fan as required at the Wilmington VA Healthcare System, located at 1601 Kirkwood HWY, Wilmington, Delaware 19805. Replace West Entrance Return Air Fan Area is located on the roof of Building 17. Work to take place during normal working hours. Provide correct size crane per lift requirements. Remove existing failed Return Air Fan. Disconnect Electrical power, control signal cabling Install new Return Air Fan ( provided by the VA). COOK Model Number 245QMXD11 900 lbs shipping weigh (see Atch 1) Properly dispose of old return air fan. Perform all necessary commissioning and startup of new equipment. All work to be performed in accordance with manufacturer s recommendations and guidelines. All Federal and State Safety and Environmental guidelines shall be followed. Work to be conducted during normal working hours. Extended hours may be arranged if necessary to fully complete performance of the work. The contractor will need to provide a certified crane operator to remove the old parts and install the new fan motor and housing parts on the roof top. Crane lift plan to be submitted, reviewed and approved by COR prior to commencement of work. Verification that return fan remains integrated into existing BAS system. Currently Johnson Controls speaking BACNET. Work to be scheduled to interfere as little as possible with normal VA operations. Crane lift is to be performed off hours to ensure that NO personnel are below the area of swing during the crane lift evolution. Other Specifics: Prime Contractor to plan all phasing of work in coordination with Hospital staff in order to minimize down-time to areas affected by the project. Construction Waste Management, Specification 01 74 19 is to be included. Prime Contractor to maintain all infection control/ dust prevention measures required. Consolidate all necessary submittals by specification section on an excel spreadsheet. Checklist to be utilized to track/ monitor submittal process. Contractor will submit picture of affected area before, during, and after construction or testing.

title: Advanced Technology Anti-Gravity Suit (ATAGS) Material Obsolescence/Prototype - RFQ
description: This Request for Quote (RFQ) is to establish a sole source contract for the Human Systems Division of the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center located at Robins Air Force Base, GA. This effort is for the procurement, construction and First Article Testing (FAT) of the Modified Advanced Technology Anti-Gravity Suit (ATAGS) which is a full coverage garment with bladders and Legacy G-Suits which is a cut-away trouser both are designed to counter G forces (or G-loc) experienced during maneuvers in high performance aircraft. AFLCMC\ROUS Body Wear IPT has identified obsolescence challenges associated with the Synergy Nomex material manufactured by Milliken and is currently used in the production of the modified ATAGS CSU-22/P and Legacy G-Suits CSU-13 B/P. To mitigate the obsolescence challenges associated with the Synergy material ROUS has discovered an alternative material that meets and/or exceeds the specification material requirements to produce ATAGS. Quantities projected and planned for this program are included in the Statement of Work (SOW), Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL), and other supporting documentation for this contract program. This effort will be executed as a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) requirements contract consisting of a one (1) year basic period, Quantities are based on Best Estimated Quantities (BEQ). The solicitation will be issued in accordance with FAR 15, Contract by Negotiation. It is anticipated that FFP will be utilized for the majority of CLINs. The overarching contract will be issued to: Vinyl Technologies LLC. (Cage: 6T584) 200 Railroad Ave, Monrovia, CA 91016 Authority 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO FAR 6.103-1, Only one responsible source, and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Specifications, plans, or drawings relating to this procurement are not available and cannot be furnished by the Government as NO TECHNICIAL DATA is available and is proprietary to the identified source above. Foreign participation is prohibited. This requirement is not a set-aside. NO HARD COPIES WILL BE PROVIDED AND NO TELEPHONE REQUESTS WILL BE HONORED. Electronic procedures will be used for this solicitation. Responsible sources may identify their interest and capability and submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. The Government does not own the data for these items. All questions and submissions to this requirement shall be submitted in writing to both of the following: Michael Carter: michael.carter.78@us.af.mil Audra Brown: audra.brown@us.af.mil All responses in reference to this synopsis shall be submitted no later than 21 December 2026, 3:00PM, EST. description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION NOTICE DESCRIPTION DETAILS The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Miami VA Healthcare System, Real Property Office, is performing market research with the intent of soliciting offers and awarding a lease with sufficient rentable square footage to yield 17,400 contiguous ABOA square feet of Medical Office and related space in Homestead, Florida. The space shall have a minimum of 150 parking spaces available. A lease up to 10 Years will be considered. New and Existing buildings will be considered. However, if not a newly constructed building, the space offered shall be in a Building that has undergone modernization, or adaptive reuse for the Space with modern conveniences and must be ready for occupancy no later than August 15, 2028. Space within or fronting on the following boundaries will be considered: North: SW 272 Street. South: SW 328 Street. East: SW 142 Avenue. West: SW 197 Avenue.. To be included in this procurement interested offerors responding to this RLP shall address ALL the following when responding to this advertisement: Cover Page contain the following information: Proposed property address with map showing property within the delineated area. Name, phone number and e-mail address of property owner. Available space. Number of parking spaces. Date space is available. Documentation evidencing that proposed property is outside the 100-year flood plain. Documentation supporting offerors ability to meet all the Government s requirements identified in this advertisement. Offers must fully comply with all requirements and supporting documentation mandatory as per the Terms and Conditions of RLP # 36C248-27-R-0012 and all exhibits attached to this announcement. All documents must be final, must be signed and must be acknowledged by placing the offeror's initials on each page. EXHIBIT M - RLP 36C248-27-R-0012 Deliverables Checklist has been included in this package to help Offerors determine the minimum documentation that needs to be included in the package. If claiming Socio-Economic status as Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB); offer must contain sufficient and clear documentation evidencing certified SDVOSB or VOSB status and must clearly show percentage of ownership and percentage of subcontracted work as well as the percentage of such work that will be done by SDVOSB or VOSB subcontractors. Any partnerships, joint ventures, or other type of associations; must clearly state and provide all documentation related to the percentage of participation of the SDVOSB or VOSB on all activities related to the lease during pre and post occupancy phases as well as percentage of ownership of the SDVOSB or VOSB firm in the partnership. If responding and you are not the property owner, i.e., broker, offer must include written signed statement from property owner (owner letterhead) authorizing you to represent the owner, in that case the offeror will be the owner, and all documentation provided must be signed by and completed accordingly. If not the owner but you responding with an offer on your behalf; the only acceptable document to demonstrate ownership/interest in the property is a notarized Purchase/Sale contract that has been signed by all parties, is not expired will remain in full force and effect and that is conditional only to the award (or not) of the lease resulting from this procurement. Any written agreement to acquire the interest may not include an option for the purchaser to assign its interest. Also, the offer must indicate that the offeror is willing to agree to include the following language in the Lease: within 30 days after execution of this Lease, Lessor will demonstrate it has obtained satisfactory title showing fee simple ownership of the property. Fee simple title must be free of any encumbrances that may limit the rights, responsibilities, or liabilities of the parties to this Lease. Lessor s failure to provide evidence of fee simple ownership within the specified timeframe shall give VA an immediate right to terminate the Lease for default. If a termination for default occurs due to the lessor s failure to provide fee simple ownership within the specific timeframe, the lessor will not be entitled to any payment whatsoever under the lease . A market survey of offered properties will be conducted by VA staff after offers have been received. Responses to this announcement are due no later than 3:00 PM ET on December 21, 2026, and must be submitted via email as follows: Department of Veterans Affairs. Office of Real Property. Attention: Javier Correa-Ochoa, Lease Contracting Officer. E-mail: javier.correaochoa@va.gov. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.5 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Cage Code/Reference Number Items - The SERVER,AUTOMATIC DA furnished under this contract/purchase order shall be the design represented by Cage Code(s) reference number(s). Cage _______ ref. no. ;1LTM5 TI20-S86-1; 3.2 Marking - This item shall be physically identified in accordance with ;MIL-STD-130, REV N, 16 NOV 2012; . 3.3 Changes in Design, Material Servicing, or Part Number - Except for a Code 1 change, which shall be processed as provided in the code statement shown below, no substitution of items shall be made until the NAVICP-MECH Contracting Officer has notified and approval has been given by issuance of a written change order. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contract
